issues.legal_issue: A document that varies an essential term of an existing registered lease must itself be registered to effect that variation.
material_facts: The lease of the land was registered and stipulated royalty rates for coke despatches.
The lessee relied on an unregistered document recording an alleged later agreement to reduce the royalty rates.
The High Court found that the alleged reduction had not been proved, and that finding was not challenged in the Supreme Court.
The Supreme Court held that, even assuming the alleged agreement had been made, the unregistered document could not effect the reduction.
issues.conclusion: The unregistered document could not vary the royalty terms of the registered lease, so the alleged reduced rates could not be relied on to defeat the claim for royalty at the lease rate.
issues.legal_principle: Under the Indian Registration Act, 1908, a document varying an essential term of an existing registered lease, including the amount payable as rent or royalty, must be registered. The Court approved Durga Prasad Singh v. Rajendra Narain Bagchi, I.L.R. 37 Cal. 293, and Lalit Mohan Ghosh v. Gopal Chuck Coal Co. Ltd., I.L.R. 39 Cal. 284, and disapproved the contrary view in Obai Goundan v. Ramalinga Ayyar, I.L.R. 22 Mad. 217.

rule.if: civil_appeal and registered_lease and unregistered_document and document_changes_essential_lease_term

predicates.civil_appeal: A party has brought a civil appeal challenging a decree concerning obligations under a lease.
predicates.registered_lease: The parties' existing lease has been registered.
predicates.unregistered_document: A document recording a later arrangement between the parties has not been registered.
predicates.document_changes_essential_lease_term: The later document purports to change an essential term of the existing lease.

issues.definition: When a civil appeal concerns a registered lease and an unregistered document purports to change an essential lease term, the change has no effect.

issues.legal_issue: An appellate challenge to a document's admissibility cannot be entertained while an unchallenged factual finding independently establishes that the alleged agreement was not proved.
material_facts: The High Court found that the alleged agreement to reduce the royalty had not been proved.
The appellant did not ask the Supreme Court to reverse that finding.
The appellant nevertheless sought to challenge the admissibility of the document recording the alleged agreement.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court would not entertain the admissibility contention while the High Court's finding that the agreement had not been proved remained undisturbed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the unchallenged factual finding as standing in the appeal and stated that the admissibility contention could not be entertained so long as that finding was not set aside.

predicates.civil_appeal: A party has brought a civil appeal from a lower court's decision.
predicates.lower_court_found_agreement_unproved: The lower court found that the agreement relied on by a party had not been proved.
predicates.finding_not_challenged: The appellant has not sought to have the finding that the agreement was unproved reversed.
predicates.appellate_admissibility_challenge_not_en: The appellate court does not entertain the admissibility challenge while the unchallenged finding remains in place.

issues.definition: When an appellant does not challenge a lower court's finding that an agreement was unproved, the appellate court does not entertain a challenge to the admissibility of the document recording that agreement while the finding stands.
